Norwegian Bliss Review

Review of Norwegian Bliss

The 2018-built Norwegian Bliss cruise ship is the 3rd of four Breakaway Plus-class NCL vessels, together with the sisterships Norwegian Escape (2015), Norwegian Joy (2017) and Norwegian Encore (2019). This class is approximately 7,000 GT larger than the previously biggest vessel in the fleet, Norwegian Epic. Bliss is NCL's 16th vessel and the 11th built by Meyer Werft (Papenburg Germany).

The vessel (IMO number 9751509) is currently Bahamas-flagged (MMSI 311000710) and registered in Nassau.

History - construction and ownership

Norwegian Cruise Line (NCL) is a subsidiary of Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Ltd (NCLH). Founded in 1966 and headquartered in Miami (Florida USA), the company is publicly traded on NASDAQ/NYSE (NYC). NCLH's major shareholders include Apollo Global Management (USA), Genting Group (Malaysia) and TPG Capital (USA). In 2017, NCL held a global cruise market share of 8.7% (passengers) and 8.4% (revenue). NCLH (the shipowner) operates the brands NCL, Oceania, and RSSC-Regent.

The 4,000-passenger Norwegian Bliss incorporates the innovative features of Norwegian Getaway and Norwegian Breakaway, along with several new interactive experiences. The vessel showcases an expanded Haven complex – the line’s “ship within a ship” concept. Accessible only by keycard, this exclusive area features an outdoor terrace, private restaurant, courtyard with retractable-roof pool, whirlpools, spa treatment rooms, sauna, and a private sundeck. Additional differences from the Breakaway class include more Haven Suites (42 increasing to 55), 26 additional Penthouses, 14 Spa Suites, and an expanded number of Studio cabins (from 59 to 82). The ship is homeported in the Port of Miami.

Decks and Cabins

Norwegian Bliss staterooms (2069 total, across 42 categories) include 1724 outside cabins, 374 Inside cabins, and 82 Studios (solo cabins).

Most staterooms measure 160-170 ft2 (15-16 m2). The ship has 1138 Balcony cabins, 111 Oceanviews and 374 Inside cabins. Wheelchair-accessible cabins number 47. The largest accommodations are The Haven Premier Owner’s Suites (1455 ft2 / 135 m2) with a wraparound terrace of 490 ft2 / 46 m2.

The 82 Studio cabins for solo travelers feature virtual views and exclusive access to the Studio Lounge. The vessel also offers many connecting staterooms suitable for families across multiple cabin categories.

The ship has 20 decks, including 16 passenger-accessible decks and 11 with cabins.

 

Shipboard dining options - Food and Drinks

Norwegian Cruise Line introduced à la carte specialty dining aboard Norwegian Bliss, allowing guests to enjoy gourmet dishes with the freedom to choose the number of courses. Norwegian Bliss offers 11 complimentary dining venues, along with numerous specialty restaurants such as Le Bistro, La Cucina, Cagney’s Steakhouse and Bayamo by James Beard Award-winning chef Jose Garces. These signature restaurants feature enhanced menus with classic favorites and new creations. Passengers can enjoy anything from a light soup to a premium dinner featuring Maine lobster, tailoring each meal to their preferences.

The ship introduces the new “Q Texas Steakhouse” (barbecue eatery with live country music) offering brisket, chicken, ribs and sausages smoked over oak, pecan and hickory. Los Lobos, a modern Mexican venue, first debuted on Norwegian Dawn in 2016.

Norwegian Bliss is the first NCL ship with a full-service Starbucks store. The first Starbucks at sea debuted in 2010 on Allure of the Seas (Royal Caribbean). Another new amenity was Coco’s, a chocolate-themed dessert venue serving pralines, crepes and truffles, paired with specialty teas and coffees. Coco's was removed during the vessel’s 2025 drydock.

Shipboard entertainment options - Fun and Sport

The Bliss features an expanded 55-suite Haven complex with a large sundeck, two whirlpools, private dining, specialty restaurants, a Thermal Suite, 14 treatment rooms (Haven Spa) and a fitness center.

NCL Bliss is the world’s second cruise ship (together with NCL Joy) to feature a Ferrari-branded racetrack (deck 19), and the first North America-based ship to offer one. Built by RiMO Supply (Germany) in partnership with Scuderia Ferrari Watches, this is also the first Formula 1-branded racetrack at sea.

  • The 2-level track spans two decks and offers ocean views from 60 m (200 ft) above sea level. Up to 10 racers can drive electric Ferrari-branded go-karts simultaneously.
  • The karts reach speeds of up to 40 mph (65 kph). Compared to Joy, Bliss’ track is 40% longer and includes 10 turns (Joy has 8), two of which extend over the side of the ship.
  • Unlimited weekly passes cost USD 100 per person; day passes cost USD 30; single rides cost USD 10. Unlimited pass holders use a separate priority line.
  • Passengers in Concierge and Haven accommodations enjoy complimentary rides. The RiMO technology ensures durability against UV exposure and saltwater conditions.

Norwegian Bliss also offers an open-air laser tag course (top deck), an Aqua Park with Double Aqua Loop (two multilevel waterslides—one extending over the hull, another with a transparent loop) and two racing slides (over 110 m / 360 ft long) with transparent sections.

Pool Deck 16 has two swimming pools positioned away from the deck’s center, plus cantilevered whirlpools extending over the ship’s sides. The kids’ water zone features splash pads, tipping buckets, water cannons and slides.

Signature activities include the two-level Ferrari go-kart track, outdoor Laser Tag Course, multistory water park, outdoor tai-chi area and luxury-brand shopping district.

Galaxy Pavilion (gaming center) features interactive video walls and Oculus VR technology. Equipment includes three XD Dark Ride motion simulators, six Xbox stations, Star Wars Battle Pod, and hovercraft bumper cars.

Itineraries

Norwegian Bliss’ itinerary program is based on weekly 7-day Alaska voyages departing Seattle, WA on Saturdays. Ports of call include Juneau, Skagway, Ketchikan and Victoria BC.

After her inaugural Alaska season, the ship was homeported in Miami, Florida for winter 2018-2019, operating 7-day Caribbean cruises visiting St Thomas (USVI), Tortola (BVI) and Nassau (Bahamas).

In January 2018, NCL announced that for winter 2019-2020, Bliss would be homeported in New York City. From NYC, she operates 18 Caribbean roundtrips ranging from 7 to 14 days, visiting ports in the Bahamas (Nassau, Great Stirrup Cay), St Lucia, St Thomas USVI, Antigua, Jamaica (Ocho Rios), Puerto Rico (San Juan), Barbados, St Maarten, St Kitts, Roatan, Mexico (Costa Maya, Cozumel) and Belize (Harvest Caye).

Norwegian Bliss Wiki

In late October 2016, Norwegian Bliss’ hull art was unveiled, themed “Cruising with the Whales.” The design is by Robert Wyland, an American artist internationally known for his large outdoor marine-life murals (“Whaling Walls”). The hull artwork features a mother humpback whale and her calf as the centerpiece, symbolizing Alaska’s natural beauty and the importance of marine conservation.

Construction officially began on October 28, 2016, with the steel-cutting ceremony. Instead of the traditional water method (injecting metal with heat), Bliss used the dry plasma cutting method, which offers higher precision and generates less debris.

The ship is equipped with the world’s largest marine scrubber system, consisting of five units manufactured and installed by Yara Marine Technologies. These scrubbers remove 99% of sulfur oxide emissions. At maximum cruising speed, the vessel’s engines consume approximately 11 tons of diesel fuel per hour. The scrubber technology reduces the equivalent of roughly 1500 tons of sulfur oxide emissions. The five in-line units are lightweight and capable of operating in dry mode as well as in open and closed loops. Additional energy-efficient technologies include heat recovery systems, LED lighting, and improved hydrodynamic hull design.

The powerplant consists of five MAN marine diesel engines (2x 14V48/60CR and 3x 12V48/60CR) with a combined output of 76.8 MW. Propulsion output totals 44 MW.

Fun facts: The vessel required approximately 300 tons of paint. The total length of onboard cabling is 2200 km (1367 miles), and the total length of piping is around 400 km (249 miles).

On May 24, 2017, the keel-laying ceremony was held at the Meyer Werft shipyard in Papenburg. During the ceremony, the first of 90 blocks was lifted into the covered construction hall. NCL’s President and CEO Andy Stuart placed a “lucky coin” beneath the block before it was lowered into position.

On November 29, 2017, NCL announced the ship’s godparent: Elvis Duran, a U.S. radio personality and host of the NYC-based Z100 morning show. The vessel’s float-out took place on February 17, 2018, and Norwegian Bliss was officially delivered to NCL on April 18, 2018.

On March 13, 2018, the ship departed Meyer Werft for its conveyance down the Ems River to Eemshaven, Holland, arriving on March 15. She was assisted by tugboats and navigated in reverse (stern first) to the North Sea for sea trials. Due to a clearance of less than 4 ft (1.2 m) through the shipyard’s sea lock, the passage took about two hours at just 0.2 knots (0.2 mph / 0.4 kph). In Eemshaven, the vessel embarked additional crew and supplies before heading to the North Sea for trials.

The official handover to NCL took place on April 19 in Bremerhaven, Germany, and the christening ceremony was held on May 30, 2018, in Seattle, WA (USA).

NCL Bliss drydock refurbishment – 2025 review

The ship’s first drydocking, conducted from January 17 to February 2, 2025, at Damen Shiprepair Brest, France, introduced several upgrades.

A new outdoor venue, Horizon Park, was added on Deck 20. Designed by SMC Design, it offers lawn-style games (such as Cornhole and Giant Jenga), a relaxation zone with sun loungers, and a stage for live entertainment.

New stateroom additions include 3-Bedroom The Haven Premiere Owner’s Suites on Deck 18 (overlooking The Haven Horizon Lounge on Deck 17), 24 Balcony staterooms, and 2 Club Balcony cabins. These were created by repurposing a section of Deck 15’s forward Observation Lounge.

Dining venue modifications on Deck 8 include Cagney’s Steakhouse (replacing Los Lobos) and Palomar, a Mediterranean seafood restaurant (replacing Ocean Blue). On Deck 6, Teppanyaki replaced Coco’s.

During the 2-day inaugural preview in NYC, Norwegian Bliss was berthed at Pier 88 in Manhattan. On May 4, the ship welcomed brand partners, U.S. media, cruise industry representatives, and godfather Elvis Duran. The Z100 morning show was broadcast live from the vessel. Following a cocktail reception in The Haven’s Horizon Lounge, VIP guests enjoyed the premiere of the “Jersey Boys” show in the Bliss Theater.

(Repositioning) 15 nights / 16 days, Inaugural Panama Canal cruise from Miami to Los Angeles – from $1350

The ship’s 2-day preview sailing from Miami (May 8–10) was an exclusive voyage for VIP guests, including Wyland (hull artist), Elvis Duran, members of The Morning Show, and Alex Vega (The Auto Firm).
